pr_title: Fix: Add Stoplight to guard erronous Web::PushSubscriptions
pr_body:
This fixes #32504, I've based it on the code for DeliveryWorker

The idea being that if a push subscription is failing continuously, we should back off and not keep retrying it for subsequent notifications.

It's worth noting this won't prevent sidekiq failures, but will drastically reduce the number of them for a badly behaving endpoint.
pr_comments:
> It's worth noting this won't prevent sidekiq failures, but will drastically reduce the number of them for a badly behaving endpoint.

It should not reduce the number of them, as Stoplight will raise an issue, and sidekiq will retry the job later as usual. However, the failure will happen immediately, without spending time querying a remote server.

> > It's worth noting this won't prevent sidekiq failures, but will drastically reduce the number of them for a badly behaving endpoint.
> 
> It should not reduce the number of them, as Stoplight will raise an issue, and sidekiq will retry the job later as usual. However, the failure will happen immediately, without spending time querying a remote server.

Oh, okay. I didn't realise stoplight would re-raise the previous error, I thought if it was in the red state, then it'd just bypass that code.

In which case, I think that yes, we need something akin to DeliveryFailureTracker for both push subscriptions and webhooks.
@renchap / @ClearlyClaire let me know if you'd like to keep this PR open or close it, as I know you've an internal ticket for webpush errors now.
As discussed, closing this as this is not the correct fix. We are investigating adding support for per-subscription rate limits

issue_context.title: Guard WebPushSubscriptions with Stoplight
issue_context.body:
### Pitch

Currently we have no handling for persistent errors with WebPush subscriptions. We should likely add stoplight code in the WebPush delivery worker like what we have in the ActivityPub delivery worker.

### Motivation

This would reduce the failure rates in redis by simply discarding the jobs when the push subscription is in an unhealthy state.
comments: +1 on this as apps are abandoned; this is really important.

review_comments: Not just 404 triggers this behaviour, but also some other 4xx errors.
It feels like we should have some tests for the "stoplight did it's thing" but I don't see any example of those in the repository.
I'm not sure if these are right for Web::PushSubscriptions, might need tuning
Is there anything we can do here for handling something like a firewall block, where the request is just dropped? This is a common failure mode for ntfy
This refactoring is based on DeliveryWorker
